rationale: The assistant sensibly ruled out blockages first and, once the customer volunteered the burning smell and sparks, immediately issued a correct stop-use/unplug instruction, refused the hose-off test, named worn brushes/commutator as the likely cause and escalated to a vacuum repair engineer. However, it never proactively asked about smells, heat, sparking or the model number despite a rough-growling 12-year-old motor, and turn 2 partly re-covered bag seating the customer had already addressed. No fabrication, no unsupported part recommendation, and calibration was appropriate ('points strongly to... commonly worn carbon brushes/commutator or a bearing/armature fault').
